INKLET GUIDES

How to sign a PDF
for free.

Add your signature to a PDF without printing or scanning. This walkthrough covers choosing your file, creating a signature, and downloading your signed copy with Inklet.

What you’ll need

A PDF file up to 25 MB and a modern web browser. You don’t need an account, a payment card, or an installed app.

Open the free PDF signing tool →
In this guide1. Choose your PDF2. Create your signature3. Place and resize it4. Download your signed PDFSigning on a phone or tabletCommon problems

1. Choose your PDF

Open the PDF signing workspace and select Choose your PDF. You can also drag a file from your computer into the drop area. Your document appears in the page preview after it opens.

Use a PDF file rather than a Word document or an image. Inklet supports files up to 25 MB. If you only want to explore the tool first, select Try a sample document to open a two-page practice PDF.

2. Draw or type your signature

Select Create signature to open the signature panel. In the Draw tab, use your mouse, trackpad, or finger to write your name. Select Clear & start fresh if you want another try.

In the Type tab, enter your name and choose Handwritten, Classic, or Elegant. Both methods offer forest green, black, and blue ink. Select That’s my signature when you’re ready to use it.

Not sure which method to choose? Our drawn and typed signature guide explains the differences.

3. Find the page and position

For a PDF with several pages, use the previous and next page arrows to find the page you want to sign. Create your signature on that page, then drag it onto the signature line or other intended area.

Adjust the Signature size slider until your mark fits. On a computer, you can also focus the signature with the keyboard and move it with the arrow keys. Hold Shift while pressing an arrow key to move it farther.

Inklet places one signature in a document at a time. To change its page, remove the current placement, navigate to the other page, and create the signature again. Check its position before downloading.

4. Download your signed PDF

Select Download PDF. Inklet creates a copy with -signed.pdf added to the file name. The signature is added to your chosen page, and the other pages remain in the downloaded document.

Open the downloaded file to review it before sharing. Your working document isn’t saved in an online account, so download your copy before closing or refreshing the page. The PDF is processed in your browser rather than uploaded to an Inklet server.

How to sign a PDF on a phone or tablet

Open Inklet in your device’s browser and choose a PDF using the file picker. After the document opens, draw with your finger or type your name. Drag the signature into place, then use Download PDF to save a signed copy.

The exact download location depends on your browser and device settings. Check the browser’s downloads list or your device’s file manager if the file doesn’t open automatically. You can use the same signing process on a desktop computer.

If your PDF won’t open or download

  • The file is too large: Reduce it below 25 MB, then choose the smaller PDF.
  • The document is protected: Password-protected or restricted PDFs may not open or save. Ask the document owner for an editable copy.
  • The download button is disabled: Create and place a signature first. Opening the document alone doesn’t enable downloading.
  • The PDF libraries didn’t load: Check your internet connection and refresh the page. Download any completed work before refreshing.
  • The recipient needs a certificate: Inklet adds a signature image. It doesn’t issue a signing certificate, verify identity, or provide an audit trail.

Signing a resume PDF?

If an employer requests a signature on your resume, keep the typed content readable and review the downloaded file before submitting it. Our ATS-friendly resume PDF guide covers text checks, application file limits, and signature placement.
